clue.text: Right idea developed with a superior accomplice

indicators.note: something developed has been worked up into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right, followed by idea as written
with means together with, as and does
a, plus better meaning superior

explanation.surface: A clever plan worked out with help from a higher-ranking partner in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase names someone who helps another commit a crime, which is exactly what an accomplice does.

clue.text: Verdict from account and the tale spun by investigators first

indicators.note: placing the detectives first means their letters come before the rearranged story

parts.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account

indicators.note: a tale that is spun is twisted round, so its letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A coroner's finding drawn from detectives' account of how the story unfolded.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged story follows AC and the detectives, who are placed in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner's court can return a finding that a death was a mishap, so the phrase is a formal ruling.

clue.text: Ideal cook?

indicators.note: to cook something is to doctor or tamper with it, so the preceding word is mixed up

parts.note: the word as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking who might be the perfect chef.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay. Delia Smith is Britain's best-known television cookery writer, often held up as the model home cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Delia Smith's recipes are trusted as foolproof in Britain, making her the archetypal model kitchen expert.

clue.text: Score with tired humour on the Mersey

definitions.note: a description of a place, standing for the town's name

parts.note: a run is a point scored in cricket
corn is stale, hackneyed humour, as in corny jokes

explanation.surface: A comedian on Merseyside scoring laughs with worn-out jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: Runcorn is an industrial town in Cheshire on the south bank of the River Mersey, the river that flows through Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The town stands on the estuary of that north-west English river, so the location phrase identifies it.

clue.text: No one takes part in what's disgusting

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
some means a part or portion of something

explanation.surface: Nobody wants to join in something revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome describes a smell or thing that is offensive and nauseating, a close synonym of revolting.

clue.text: Still having doctor in charge after drink

indicators.note: coming after means these pieces are placed behind the word for a drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A doctor still on duty after having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning even now, but it is the noun: the apparatus used for distilling.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling vessel, and a still is the apparatus for distilling spirits.

clue.text: A little engraving by an artist — one that will last

parts.note: a little of the word engraving: just its opening two letters
Albrecht Dürer, the German Renaissance painter and engraver

explanation.surface: A small engraved print made by a famous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Dürer was best known for his engravings, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who endures is a person or thing that keeps going and survives hardship over time.

clue.text: Skilled hand — and master, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words are one possible arrangement of letters that could be reordered

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman who might also be a master of his craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a worker such as a plumber or joiner trained in a manual craft, so a skilled worker.

clue.text: Withhold donation for one who calls for a tip

definitions.text: one who calls for a tip

parts.note: to withhold something is to refuse it
a collector is the person who gathers donations

explanation.surface: Refusing to give money to someone who comes asking for a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip seems to be a gratuity, but it is also the rubbish dump; British binmen traditionally call at houses for a Christmas tip too.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustman visits homes to take away rubbish, which is then carted off to the municipal dump.

clue.text: Wild flower also gathered by Dion

indicators.note: what is gathered is held in, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: Céline Dion, the Canadian singer
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A singer collecting a wild bloom as well.
explanation.definitionFit: The celandine is a small yellow plant of hedgerows and woods, a common uncultivated bloom.

clue.text: Very little hostility between Germany and France

indicators.note: something between two things is placed in the middle of them

parts.note: D is Germany's international vehicle code, from Deutschland
war is open hostility
F is France's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Hardly any conflict between two neighbouring European nations.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective dwarf means much smaller than normal, as in dwarf conifers, so tiny.

clue.text: Topping game involves one in a blood transfusion

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one letter is drawn inside the others
a transfusion moves blood about, so these letters are poured into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A first-rate pastime involving someone receiving blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' seems to mean excellent, but it is literal: diabolo is played with a spinning top, a double cone whirled on a string between two sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling pastime in which a two-headed spinning top is tossed and caught on a string.

clue.text: Spy may have been granted freedom

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Guy ..., one of the Cambridge spies who fled to Moscow
second meaning: a freeman or citizen of a borough

explanation.surface: A spy who might have been released.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pardoned agent; the second sense is the old title for a citizen holding the freedom of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgess was a borough citizen with full municipal rights, and Guy Burgess was a famous Soviet agent.

clue.text: African leader is number one in France

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Daniel arap ..., long-serving president of Kenya
second meaning: the French word for me, oneself

explanation.surface: An African statesman is the top figure in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' means oneself, so in French it is the word for me.
explanation.definitionFit: Moi was Kenya's head of state from 1978 to 2002, and the French pronoun refers to the speaker himself.

clue.text: Hole in one — possibly secures appointment

definitions.note: a noun for the post, standing for the person put forward for it

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the word as written, to be rearranged
a mine is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: A golfer's hole in one might win someone a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is the candidate proposed for an office or post, the person behind an appointment.

clue.text: Politician misled into taking mansion I had to leave?

indicators.note: going into something taking it in places one part inside another
having to leave means a letter departs from the word

parts.note: taken as written
the letter removed
read as mis-led: the word led put wrong, its letters back to front

explanation.surface: A politician led astray into acquiring a grand house he then had to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mandelson resigned from the Cabinet in 1998 over a loan to buy his house, which gives the question mark its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mandelson was a leading Labour figure and Cabinet minister under Tony Blair.

clue.text: Wool producer in the Western Isles

indicators.note: in tells you the letters are sitting inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Sheep farming in the islands off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep grows a fleece that is shorn for its fibre, so it yields the raw material of yarn.

clue.text: Ice cream production out east in China

indicators.note: production makes something new from raw material, so the letters are reworked
out means removed, so this letter is taken away

parts.note: the letters of both words
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Making ice cream in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fine porcelain, a type of fired clay ware, which is what ceramic means as a noun or adjective.

clue.text: Wood father left from cutting up maple

indicators.note: what has left from a word is no longer part of it
in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad has gone off sawing up a maple tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood tree, and its timber is used for furniture and coffins.

clue.text: Cockney isn't ever turning poetic, of course

parts.note: ain't is the dialect form a Londoner might use

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read back to front

parts.note: e'er is the contracted form of ever found in verse
tells you to use the verse form of the previous word

explanation.surface: A Londoner insisting he never turns to poetry, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as a phrase meaning naturally; here course is the definition. Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse that stages the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is the famous horse-racing venue, a racetrack being a course.

clue.text: No end of a true blue property dealer

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: real means true, genuine
blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, the Tories

explanation.surface: A loyal Conservative who deals in property, and no end of one.
explanation.walkthrough: Realtor is the American word for an estate agent.
explanation.definitionFit: In US English a realtor is an agent who buys and sells houses and land for clients.

clue.text: Aim to love and marry with a dowry

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: Setting out to love and marry with money in the bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Endowed means provided with money or property, as a bride brought a sum to the marriage.

clue.text: False plea men put to a jury

indicators.note: something false is not as it should be, so the letters are wrongly ordered

parts.note: the letters of these words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Men enter a dishonest plea before a jury.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts a case to the jury; the definition means appointing people to serve on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To empanel is to enrol people as jurors, assigning them to serve on a panel in court.

clue.text: Communication that is spelt incorrectly

indicators.note: spelt incorrectly suggests letters in the wrong order

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A message with spelling mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, a written message sent to someone.

clue.text: Blair gets quiet reminder, no date excluded

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: excluded means left out, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
n.d. is the bibliographic abbreviation for no date

explanation.surface: Tony Blair is quietly reminded that no dates are excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was British Prime Minister from 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Blair was head of the British government, whose title is commonly shortened to first minister in that sense.

clue.text: A little drink — about 4 1/2 gallons!

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pin is an old cask measure of four and a half gallons

explanation.surface: A small drink that turns out to be over four gallons.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark enjoys the contrast: a tiny drink from a hefty cask.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small measure of spirits, a quick tot or sip.

clue.text: Stamp severely on a Conservative?

parts.note: a die is a stamp for impressing coins or medals
hard means severely, as in hit hard

explanation.surface: Trampling hard on a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamp' looks like a verb; here it is the noun for a tool that impresses a design.
explanation.definitionFit: A diehard is a stubborn reactionary resisting all change, so a type of traditional Tory, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Treat that's difficult to repeat

indicators.note: something difficult is awkward or troublesome, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A treat that is hard to have again.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say something again, a formal synonym of the verb meaning go over once more.

clue.text: Crooked like a botanical garden

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
Kew Gardens in London is the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: A garden as bent and twisted as a botanical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means at an angle or out of line, not straight, the same as bent or crooked.

clue.text: Withdrawal of saving scheme is an advantage

indicators.note: a withdrawal draws something back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a TESSA was a Tax-Exempt Special Savings Account, a UK savings plan of the 1990s

explanation.surface: Taking money out of a savings plan turns out to be beneficial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawal' suggests taking cash out of an account, which fits the savings scheme in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something useful or valuable, a benefit or plus point.

clue.text: Not the setting for a dry run

definitions.text: Not the setting for a dry run

parts.words: Not the setting for a dry run
parts.note: surface reading: somewhere unsuitable for a rehearsal or practice session
setter's reading: in cricket, a damp rain-soaked pitch is no place for runs scored in dry conditions

explanation.walkthrough: A dry run is a rehearsal, but read literally it is a cricket run scored on dry ground; the answer is a rain-soaked cricket pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain-damaged cricket pitch is the opposite of dry, so it cannot host scoring in dry conditions.

clue.text: Vandal turned out drawers ready for a long engagement

parts.note: the Vandals and the Huns were both barbarian peoples who sacked Rome, and Hun is used for any destroyer

indicators.note: drawers that are turned out are emptied and jumbled, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A burglar empties out the drawers, ready for a lengthy stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' suggests a betrothal, but it is a battle; the war between England and France ran from 1337 to 1453.
explanation.definitionFit: The conflict lasted well over a century, so it is a very protracted military engagement.
